articles.title: Agentic Reasoning for Large Language Models
articles.summary: A survey arguing that LLMs reason well in closed settings but struggle in open-ended, dynamic ones, motivating a shift to treating them as agents that plan, act, and learn through interaction. It organizes the field into three layers: foundational single-agent reasoning, self-evolving agents that refine via feedback and memory, and collective multi-agent collaboration.

articles.title: Gate-Drain Leakage Enhanced by Drain-Induced Dielectric Barrier Lowering in Gate-All-Around FETs
articles.summary: Sandia researchers use first-principles simulations to trace the off-state leakage in gate-all-around FETs at negative gate voltage to gate-to-drain tunneling, significantly enhanced by drain-induced dielectric barrier lowering. Pinning down this mechanism matters for the scaling limits and off-state current of the GAA nodes now entering high-volume production.

articles.title: EnzyPGM: Pocket-conditioned Generative Model for Substrate-specific Enzyme Design
articles.summary: Proposes EnzyPGM, a generative model that jointly designs an enzyme and its substrate-binding pocket, conditioned on the target substrate and functional priors, with attention modules that model fine-grained pocket-residue-to-substrate-atom interactions earlier methods captured poorly. The authors also curate EnzyPock, a dataset of 83,062 enzyme-substrate pairs across 1,036 enzyme families.

articles.title: SAGE: Synthetic Aging for a Grid Environment
articles.summary: Introduces SAGE, an open-source, physics-informed framework that generates hour-resolved, multi-decade operating and degradation histories for heterogeneous grid-battery fleets under realistic market dispatch, coupling electro-thermal behavior with calendar and cycle aging. It gives degradation-aware algorithms and digital twins the long-horizon, physically consistent ground truth that lab cycling and proprietary field data lack.

articles.title: The Future of Warfare: National Positions on the Governance of Lethal Autonomous Weapons Systems
articles.summary: Analyzes recent international diplomacy on lethal autonomous weapons, now reaching the battlefield, and sorts national positions into three camps: traditionalists who rely on existing international law, prohibitionists who seek a ban, and dualists who want a new treaty banning some uses while regulating others. It then identifies potential next steps for governance.

articles.title: Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computing with Trapped Ions: The Walking Cat Architecture
articles.summary: Presents the 'walking cat' fault-tolerant architecture for trapped ions, built entirely on quantum low-density parity-check (LDPC) codes, with a full stack: compiler, error-correction protocols, micro-architecture, a fast decoder, and detailed simulations. Its backbone is a 'cat factory' that produces cat states distributed across the machine and consumes them to perform logical operations.

articles.title: AI-Guided Computational Design of a Room-Temperature, Ambient-Pressure Superconductor Candidate: Grokene
articles.summary: Uses an LLM-guided discovery workflow, paired with first-principles many-body calculations, to propose Grokene, a graphene-derived 2D superlattice with a predicted mean-field critical temperature near 310-325 K at ambient pressure. Its strictly 2D nature introduces phase fluctuations that cap the observable monolayer transition near 120 K, which stacking, gating, or doping might raise.

articles.title: Multilinguality of Large Language Models From a Structural Perspective
articles.summary: Uses representational structural analysis to probe how LLMs internally organize different languages. The authors find that low-resource languages sit structurally farther from English than high- and mid-resource ones, and that language-specific post-training reshapes a language's internal structure while largely preserving its relationships to other languages.

articles.title: Chips in the Flatland: 2D Semiconductors for Future Computing Electronics
articles.summary: A review arguing that as silicon transistor scaling nears its physical limits in the Angstrom era, atomically thin 2D semiconductors have emerged as leading candidate channel materials. It connects material- and device-level breakthroughs to circuit- and chip-level design, mapping what is still needed to move 2D electronics from lab demonstrations toward manufacturable computing hardware.

articles.title: An accurate nucleic acid-small molecule docking framework via geometric deep learning with large-scale pretraining
articles.summary: Introduces a geometric deep-learning model, pretrained at large scale, that predicts how small molecules bind to nucleic acids such as RNA and DNA rather than the usual protein targets. On an external benchmark of 125 nucleic acid-ligand complexes it reached a 56% docking success rate, pointing toward drug discovery against RNA targets that are difficult to drug by conventional means.

articles.title: Dynamic resource coordination can increase grid hosting capacity to support more renewables, storage, and electrified load growth
articles.summary: Models how coordinating distributed energy resources in real time, instead of relying on static interconnection limits, changes how much clean technology a distribution grid can absorb. The authors find dynamic coordination can support up to 200% solar, 100% battery, and 90% heat-pump penetration while cutting solar curtailment, easing a key bottleneck to electrification.

articles.title: Algorethics and Neuro-Symbolic Military AI: Ontologies, "Hellscapes," Just War, and Silicon Valley
articles.summary: A policy and ethics paper examining how neuro-symbolic AI is being applied to military command and autonomous weapons, and the governance gaps this creates. It weighs the technology against just-war principles and the expanding role of commercial technology firms in defense, arguing for explicit ethical constraints—'algorethics'—designed into such systems.

articles.title: Quantum error correction with the toric code
articles.summary: Demonstrates many repeated rounds of error correction on a neutral-atom processor running the toric code, using mid-circuit measurement and replacement of lost atoms with freshly initialized qubits. Logical information survived up to 90 correction cycles, and a companion repetition-code memory preserved encoded data for about a minute—far longer than any single atom—showing error correction that scales to arbitrary depth.

articles.title: Superheating field of clean superconductors near the type-I--type-II boundary: the low-temperature Meissner stability limit of niobium
articles.summary: Uses self-consistent Eilenberger theory and a linear stability analysis to calculate the maximum field a clean superconductor can sustain in its Meissner state, focusing on niobium near the type-I/type-II boundary. For niobium-like parameters it predicts a superheating field near 290 mT at low temperature, setting a fundamental limit relevant to the performance of superconducting radio-frequency accelerator cavities.

articles.title: Agentic Transformers Provably Learn to Search via Reinforcement Learning
articles.summary: A theory paper studying how transformer policies acquire search behavior when trained with reinforcement learning. The authors show that tree-search-like strategies can provably emerge from sparse reward signals during training, offering a mathematical account of why agentic models learn to explore and backtrack rather than just memorize answers.

articles.title: Thermal Processing Limits in Oxide-Channel Ferroelectric Field Effect Transistors
articles.summary: Systematically studies how high-temperature post-capping anneals affect the memory behavior of oxide-semiconductor-channel ferroelectric FETs built on a Hf0.5Zr0.5O2 gate stack with an HfO2 capping layer. By mapping the thermal-budget window that preserves device performance, the work informs how these emerging non-volatile memory transistors can be integrated into back-end-of-line manufacturing flows.

articles.title: Single-Cell Cross-Modal Transfer by Adversarial Fine-Tuning of Foundation Models
articles.summary: Shows that a single-cell foundation model can be adversarially fine-tuned to translate between biological data modalities, helping bridge the gap between bulk and spatial transcriptomics. The approach aims to profile many thousands of genes at subcellular resolution, supporting tissue analyses that depend on cellular structure, proximity, and interaction.

articles.title: Artificial Intelligence for Instability in Inorganic Perovskites: From Mechanism Discovery to Engineering Strategies
articles.summary: Reviews how AI can tackle the instability that still limits inorganic perovskite solar cells under thermal, chemical, optical, and electrical stress. The authors argue an integrated approach is needed because the design space spans composition, additives, processing, interfaces, and encapsulation, with targets including not just efficiency but lifetime, reproducibility, and manufacturability.

articles.title: AI-Enabled Military Decision-Making and Escalation Risk: Human-Machine Command Authority in Great Power Competition
articles.summary: Argues that while high autonomy may be warranted in narrow tasks such as missile defense and hypersonic intercept, delegating command authority to AI in ambiguous or nuclear-adjacent situations undermines crisis stability. It compares US, Chinese, and Russian approaches to human-machine command and the escalation risks each creates in great-power competition.

articles.title: Correlation-Assisted Odd-Parity Encoded Gates in Coupled Fluxonium Qubits under Non-Markovian TLS Noise
articles.summary: Proposes encoding two-qubit gates in the odd-parity subspace of coupled fluxonium qubits to make them more resilient to non-Markovian noise from two-level-system defects. By exploiting noise correlations rather than fighting them, the scheme aims to raise gate fidelity in fluxonium processors, an increasingly competitive alternative to transmon-based superconducting hardware.

articles.title: Six Open Questions in Machine-Learned Interatomic Potential Foundation Models
articles.summary: A perspective on the shift toward 'foundational' machine-learned interatomic potentials—large pretrained models meant to predict atomic forces across much of the periodic table. It lays out six open questions about their accuracy, transferability, and evaluation, framing what the materials-modeling community still needs to resolve before these models can be trusted as general-purpose tools.

articles.title: WorldReasoner: Evaluating Whether Language Model Agents Forecast Events with Valid Reasoning
articles.summary: Introduces a benchmark of 345 resolved forecasting tasks, with causal graphs spanning 8,087 events, to test not just whether language-model agents predict the future accurately but whether they reason validly in doing so. The authors find that temporally valid retrieval is the strongest driver of accuracy and that building causal graphs improves recovery of the key events behind an outcome.

articles.title: Breaking the width-scaling limit in high-performance atomically thin 2D nanoribbon transistors
articles.summary: Reducing transistor channel width below 40-50 nm has been a bottleneck because edge disorder and lateral depletion sap drive current. Using atomically thin MoS2 nanoribbon transistors scaled to 15 nm, the authors instead see on-current density rise by up to 230% (monolayer) and 170% (bilayer), while keeping record on/off ratios—overturning the usual width-scaling penalty.

articles.title: AgentPLM: Agentic Protein Language Models with Reasoning-Augmented Decoding for Protein Sequence Design
articles.summary: Reframes protein language models as agents that consult external biophysical feedback while decoding, rather than generating sequences passively in one pass. This reasoning-augmented decoding lets the model steer designs toward better structural and functional properties, aiming to improve the reliability of computational protein sequence design.

articles.title: Learning-Assisted Day-Ahead Energy Scheduling for Frequency-Secure Inverter-Dominated Grids with Grid-Forming Battery Storage
articles.summary: Proposes a learning-assisted day-ahead scheduling framework that uses a surrogate model to capture the frequency-support dynamics of grid-forming battery storage. This sidesteps the electromagnetic-transient simulations normally too costly to embed in grid optimization, helping operators schedule inverter-dominated, renewable-heavy grids while keeping frequency secure.

articles.title: Appropriate Human Judgement: U.S. Policy on Lethal Autonomous Weapons Systems and the Law of Armed Conflict
articles.summary: Examines the U.S. requirement (DODI 3000.09) for 'appropriate levels of human judgement' over lethal autonomous weapons and what it demands of commanders under the law of armed conflict. It works through how that standard maps onto targeting obligations as autonomous systems move closer to fielding.

articles.title: Coherent versus stochastic error injection on a repetition-code logical qubit in superconducting hardware
articles.summary: Uses a bit-flip repetition code on a transmon processor as a testbed to compare how coherent versus stochastic physical errors propagate to logical performance. Distinguishing these error types matters because they degrade error-corrected qubits differently, informing how real hardware noise should be modeled and suppressed.

articles.title: DPA4: Pushing the Accuracy-Cost Frontier of Interatomic Potentials with EMFA SO(2) Convolution
articles.summary: Presents DPA4, an equivariant machine-learned interatomic-potential architecture whose new SO(2) convolution and training path cut the heavy compute cost of expressive models, with about a 3x speedup. On the Matbench Discovery benchmark its compact 2.76M-parameter variant beats a 30M-parameter baseline, pushing the accuracy-versus-cost frontier for atomistic materials simulation.

articles.title: LLM Consortium for Software Design Refinement: A Controlled Experiment on Multi-Agent Collaboration Topologies
articles.summary: A controlled experiment compares 12 ways of wiring multiple LLM agents together for software architecture design, running 520 trials across 8 tasks and scoring them with three independent automated evaluators. It finds that an adversarial setup demanding full rewrites ranks best, and that cross-model review—generating with one model and reviewing with another—is a consistent runner-up.

articles.title: Solid-state transcapacitor: a new gain element for logic, memory and interconnects
articles.summary: Proposes the 'transcapacitor,' a solid-state gain element intended to address the energy-scaling limits of conventional transistors across logic, memory, and interconnects. The work frames it as a candidate building block for more energy-efficient electronics as traditional device scaling slows.

articles.title: ProHiFlo: Hierarchical Flow Matching with Functional Guidance for De Novo Protein Generation
articles.summary: Introduces ProHiFlo, a hierarchical flow-matching generative model for designing proteins from scratch with explicit functional guidance. On the task of scaffolding enzyme active sites it reports a 58.9% success rate, well above the 41.2% of the RFDiffusion baseline, pointing toward more reliable de novo design for enzyme engineering and therapeutics.

articles.title: Energy Storage as a Multi-Use Asset: Applications Across the Power System
articles.summary: Surveys how a single energy-storage asset can serve many roles across the power system, from short-duration services like frequency regulation and voltage support to longer-duration peak shaving and seasonal buffering. It frames storage as flexible infrastructure for offsetting renewable variability rather than a single-purpose device.

articles.title: Artificial Intelligence in Future Warfare: Ethical Frameworks and the Regulation of Lethal Autonomous Weapons
articles.summary: Argues that AI has compressed the lethal decision cycle from hours to milliseconds, outpacing the international law meant to constrain it. The paper surveys nine real-world autonomous-weapon systems, classifies each by how much human control remains (in-, on-, or out-of-the-loop), and proposes regulation calibrated to the actual risk of autonomous lethality.

articles.title: Approximating optimal decoding of quantum LDPC codes with narrow frontiers
articles.summary: Presents the 'Frontier' decoder, a pruned dynamic-programming method for quantum LDPC codes that keeps only a narrow set of the most promising decoding states instead of the full exponential search. It reaches near-optimal thresholds for surface and color codes and state-of-the-art accuracy on the gross code while retaining a very small candidate list.

articles.title: Density-wave order enhances the phonon thermal Hall effect in a trilayer nickelate
articles.summary: Reports a phonon thermal Hall effect in the trilayer nickelate La4Ni3O10 that is strongly enhanced below its density-wave transition near 140 K, showing two distinct plateaus. The extracted energy scale matches a magnon-phonon crossing, pointing to magnon-phonon hybridization as the mechanism—insight into a family of materials tied to high-temperature superconductivity.

articles.title: Large Language Models Hack Rewards, and Society
articles.summary: Argues that societal regulations resemble reward functions—measurable outcomes and thresholds that leave institutional intent only partly specified—and asks whether LLMs' tendency to hack reward functions during RL training can scale up to 'societal hacking.' Using SocioHack, a sandbox of 72 societal environments, the authors find models do learn to discover regulatory loopholes that stay technically compliant while defeating the rules' intent, and that current safeguards only partially catch it.

articles.title: Programmable Probabilistic Computer with 1,000,000 p-bits
articles.summary: Builds a probabilistic computer with one million p-bits by networking many FPGAs into a single Ising machine, breaking past the single-chip capacity and memory-bandwidth limits that had capped earlier p-bit hardware. The system performs Gibbs sampling at over a trillion flips per second while keeping every coupling weight in local on-chip memory, a step toward dedicated hardware accelerators for large-scale sampling and combinatorial optimization.

articles.title: Protein Dynamics Beyond Structure Prediction
articles.summary: Argues that despite AlphaFold-class successes at predicting static protein structures, how sequences give rise to dynamic conformational changes and assemblies remains largely unsolved. The paper reviews single-molecule techniques that observe folding trajectories in real time alongside new computational and data-driven methods, making the case for shifting the field from static structural endpoints toward mechanistic models of folding dynamics in living cells.

articles.title: Rethinking the green power grid for stability, not just for climate
articles.summary: Pushes back on the assumption that renewable-heavy grids are inherently less stable, arguing that renewable generation can actually strengthen grid stability through synthetic inertia, advanced inverter-based control, and coordinated transmission planning. It frames rapid advances in energy storage and power electronics as making a stability-first, not just climate-first, case for the renewable transition.

articles.title: The Drone Debates: Rethinking How Emerging Military Technologies Shape Power
articles.summary: Revisits a decade of drone-warfare punditry against the actual record, questioning claims that cheap autonomous drones are radically redistributing military power toward smaller states and non-state actors. The authors, leading scholars of military technology and international politics, argue for a more careful framework for judging which emerging technologies genuinely reshape power balances versus which just generate hype.

articles.title: Repetition-code-based readout error detection and correction across hardware platforms and generations
articles.summary: Benchmarks the same repetition-code readout-error detection and correction protocol across IBM's Heron r1-r3 superconducting processors and Quantinuum's H1 and H2 trapped-ion processors. Redundantly encoding each data qubit with ancillas before measurement and decoding by post-selection or majority voting improves readout fidelity on every device and hardware generation tested, even as unencoded baselines kept improving on their own.

articles.title: Facet-selective ballistic supercurrent in a weak topological insulator
articles.summary: Demonstrates Josephson junctions built on the weak topological insulator ZrTe5 in which the supercurrent concentrates on specific crystallographic facets that host gapless topological surface states. Superconducting quantum interferometry shows SQUID-like critical-current oscillations with flux-quantum periodicity, realizing in a 3D crystal a facet-selective surface supercurrent that had previously only been achieved with 1D edge modes in 2D systems—a building block for topological superconductivity.

articles.title: Message Passing Enables Efficient Reasoning
articles.summary: Tackles the computational bottleneck of long chain-of-thought reasoning by letting parallel LLM threads talk to each other directly. The proposed Message Passing Language Models add lightweight send and receive primitives so threads share only what matters and can terminate early on partial results from peers, improving on fork-join parallel scaling where threads stay isolated.

articles.title: GaN Power Devices and Converter Architectures for AI Data Centers: Efficiency, Reliability, and Deployment Pathways
articles.summary: Reviews how gallium-nitride power transistors fit the escalating power-delivery demands of AI data centers, mapping Si, SiC, and GaN against converter-relevant metrics across each stage from front-end power-factor correction to point-of-load regulation. It concludes GaN offers a stage-dependent rather than universal advantage, with mature lateral GaN HEMTs most effective in high-frequency, low-to-mid-voltage stages where switching losses dominate.

articles.title: BioMatrix: Towards a Comprehensive Biological Foundation Model Spanning the Modality Matrix of Sequences, Structures, and Language
articles.summary: Introduces BioMatrix, a single decoder-only foundation model that natively handles molecule and protein sequences, 3D structures, and natural language in one shared token space, avoiding the separate encoders most biological models rely on. Built on Qwen3 and continually pretrained on 304 billion tokens, it aims to unify broad entity coverage with true multimodality under a single next-token objective for tasks across drug and protein design.

articles.title: Mobility-safe adaptive reserve certification for EV–hydrogen-bus–building resilience hubs
articles.summary: Proposes a scheduling framework for zero-emission depots that combine EV charging, hydrogen buses, and backup power for critical buildings, where hydrogen sent to a building could otherwise strand buses. Using a physics-hybrid building-load model and conformal reserve calibration that adapts to seasonal drift, it enforces a mobility-first rule that protects post-disaster bus service before allocating hydrogen to buildings, treating these sites as grid resilience assets.

articles.title: Governing Military Artificial Intelligence Technologies: Manufacturing War or Peace with Artificial Intelligence
articles.summary: Uses BERTopic natural-language-processing over 505 papers from 2014–2025 to systematically map the decade of scholarship on military AI. The review distills the literature into three spectra and six sub-themes—governance (national strategy, rules and ethics), application (regional security, social and cultural influences), and technology (tactics, logistics)—offering a structured picture of where military-AI research has concentrated and where gaps remain.

articles.title: Bias-Preserving Gates and Quantum Error Correction With Dual-Rail Cat Codes
articles.summary: Proposes the dual-rail cat code, a concatenated bosonic encoding that nests an inner cat code inside an outer dual-rail structure to inherit the strengths of both. The dual-rail layer converts photon-loss errors into detectable erasures, while the cat layer supplies resource-efficient, bias-preserving logical gates—combining efficient photon-loss handling with bias-tailored error correction that each encoding lacks on its own.

articles.title: Ising superconductivity and anomalous metallic states in a bulk crystal with artificial unidirectional stacking layers
articles.summary: Reports a synthesized Sr0.75ClNbS2 crystal that forces all NbS2 layers into a parallel AA stacking never before realized in bulk, using a planar Sr-Cl network to reorganize the structure rather than just expand layer spacing. Breaking inversion symmetry this way reproduces an isolated monolayer's electronic environment in three dimensions, preventing cancellation of the local Ising fields and yielding bulk Ising superconductivity plus anomalous metallic states.
